newsitem.title: UK: Britain's new prime minister forges ruling team.
newsitem.headline: Britain's new prime minister forges ruling team.

text.p: Prime Minister Tony Blair on Saturday carried out the promise he made after his Labour Party's landslide general election victory to replace talking with action, summoning minister after minister to complete his cabinet.
Blair, who will be 44 on Tuesday and is Britain's youngest prime minister in 185 years, gave a clear signal he intends to make a radical start after 18 unbroken years of Conservative Party rule.
Marjorie "Mo" Mowlam, a pugnacious politician who has just survived treatment for a benign brain tumour, was named Northern Ireland secretary and flew straight to Belfast to get down to work.
She faces a tough task to rescue a stalled process to bring peace to the British-ruled province and find a solution to a sectarian conflict rooted in history and steeped in blood.

Leftwinger Clare Short, an outspoken politician whose prospects appeared at risk after loose talking on tax and legalising cannabis, also made the cabinet as overseas development secretary, confounding political commentators who thought she would be left out.

Blair named Harriet Harman as social security secretary and Ann Taylor as leader of the House of Commons (lower house), a key parliamentary job, taking the number women members to five, three more than in John Major's ousted government.
The sober reality of government contrasted with the euphoria which greeted Blair's victory in Thursday's election.

Thousands of supporters danced through the night into Friday morning as results confirmed the demise of Conservative rule. Crowds dizzy with joy at Labour Party's biggest election victory cheered and sang as Blair arrived at 10 Downing Street, the prime ministerial residence, on Friday afternoon with his family.

Blair's young family -- his daughter Kathryn is nine and his sons Nicky and Euan, 11 and 13 respectively -- grappled on Saturday with the problem of where to live after their father's stunning victory.
Aides said Blair and his wife, Cherie, had ruled out living above the Downing Street office because the apartment quarters were too limited for space.
They now are looking at the larger flat next door, above the house that is traditionally occupied by the finance minister.

Cherie, a high-flying lawyer who sacrificed her own political ambitions for her husband and who is likely to continue with her career, arrived at Downing Street at lunchtime on Saturday saying she was just getting used to the change in her life.
Blair arrived several hours earlier to shape the team to translate his promised new dawn for Britain into reality.
Blair has already appointed deputy Labour Party leader John Prescott as deputy prime minister.

Gruff Scot Gordon Brown becomes chancellor of the exchequer (finance minister), another Scot, Robin Cook, takes over as foreign secretary and Britain's first blind minister will be education secretary David Blunkett.
Blair on Saturday signalled his determination to devolve power from London by naming Donald Dewar as Scottish secretary.

A surprise appointment of Frank Field -- a radical thinker on pensions -- as a minister in the social security department, a post just outside the cabinet, also signalled his intention to carry out a root-and-branch reform of the welfare system.
Pensions became a key campaign issue with Labour accusing the Conservatives of threatening to ditch universal state pensions.
The crucial importance of devolving power to Scotland -- an issue which brought down the last Labour government in 1979 -- is seen as requiring all of Dewar's wily parliamentary skills.
Other MPs expected to be confirmed in the cabinet later is Chris Smith, the only member of Blair's team who has avowed his homosexuality, and Scot George Robertson as defence secretary.
As Labour busied itself with government, shell-shocked Conservatives called for a period of calm before elections for a new leader to replace John Major, who announced on Friday he was stepping down.
But former finance minister Kenneth Clarke has already thrown his hat into the ring and other possible contenders were circling, awaiting the right moment to declare their eligibility.
